GlobalForge Equipment Inc. - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalForge Equipment Inc. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GlobalForge Equipment's results for the Q3. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on GlobalForge Equipment's performance for the Q3. We've made significant progress on several fronts, delivering adjusted EPS of $1.82, up 14% year-over-year, with our book-to-bill ratio holding steady at 1.25x across our core CNC machining and automation segments. Our record backlog has grown 11% to $4.2 billion, reflecting strong demand in renewables, aerospace, and semiconductors. We've successfully closed key acquisitions like RoboTech Dynamics, bolstering our collaborative robotics capabilities, and announced bolt-ons in forgings and hydraulics to drive vertical integration and geographic diversification. Revenue grew 12% year-over-year, fueled by aftermarket services and reshoring trends, while our supply chain initiatives have compressed lead times and enhanced resilience.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives—'Forge Forward' for technology tuck-ins, sustainability through CO2 reductions, and capacity expansions in Ohio and Mexico—are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth amid Industry 4.0 shifts.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Sarah. Turning to our financial performance, GlobalForge Equipment reported $1.28 billion in revenue for the Q3, representing a 12% increase year-over-year and 5% sequentially from Q2. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of organic growth, driven by that 1.25x book-to-bill and the record $4.2 billion backlog, up 18% YoY. Gross margin was 38.2%, expanding on higher service attach rates and pricing discipline, though pressured 120 basis points by component cost inflation. Operating expenses were $420 million, reflecting targeted investments in R&D and supply chain resilience, resulting in operating income of $245 million. Our net income for the quarter was $180 million, or $1.82 adjusted EPS per share.

Let me break down revenue performance by geographic region, as this underscores the resilience and diversification of our portfolio in the industrial equipment sector. Our revenue mix reflects ongoing structural shifts—reshoring in North America, supply chain diversification, and accelerating Industry 4.0 adoption like our IoT-enabled CNC machining centers and collaborative robotic arms. Aftermarket services, including predictive maintenance via our Forge Cloud platform, contributed 28% of total revenue, up from 24% a year ago, providing high-margin visibility amid cyclical fluctuations.

North America accounted for 45% of revenue at $576 million, up 18% YoY and 7% sequentially. This is our largest and highest-growth region, fueled by domestic manufacturing resurgence. U.S. revenue grew 20% to $520 million, benefiting from CHIPS Act-driven semiconductor fab expansions and EV production ramps among OEMs like Tesla and GM suppliers. Our PrecisionForge high-speed milling machines saw 35% uptake as customers prioritize onshoring to mitigate tariffs and disruptions. Canada added $56 million, up 12%, with aerospace aftermarket strength for Boeing and Bombardier. Margins expanded 220 basis points to 28% on remote diagnostics that cut unplanned downtime by 25%. We're investing $150 million in our Ohio facility to boost capacity for palletizing robots, aiming for a 2-point market share gain.

Europe represented 28% of revenue, or $358 million, up 5% YoY but flat sequentially, amid energy crises and softening automotive demand. Germany and the Nordics drove 60% of the segment at $215 million, up 8%, on battery gigafactory equipment for Volkswagen and Northvolt. Our EcoDrive systems, compliant with EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, secured $120 million in orders. Southern Europe grew just 1% to $143 million, hit by Fiat Chrysler inventory and French slowdowns. FX shaved 2 points off growth, offset by 15% aftermarket gains from PLC upgrades. We're optimistic on wind turbine recovery, with 80% of 2024 exposures hedged.

Asia-Pacific delivered 22% of revenue, $282 million, up 15% YoY and 8% sequentially, driven by semiconductor and electronics capex. China hit $140 million, up 22% despite export controls, as SMIC ramps 28nm production with our etching tools. India surged 45% to $65 million on 'Make in India' for Foxconn and Tata EVs—we shipped first FlexiBot units. Southeast Asia grew 10% to $77 million on Malaysian HDD for Seagate. Softening solar in China was offset by medtech pivots; margins hit 26% with 40% ASEAN sourcing, cutting lead times 30%.

Rest of World was 5%, $64 million, up 10% YoY. Latin America grew 14% to $32 million on Brazilian agribusiness and Mexican nearshoring; Middle East/Africa added $32 million on Saudi Aramco upgrades with explosion-proof welders. Digital twins cut deployment costs 20%.

This diversification—no region over 45%—de-risks volatility, with balanced end-markets: 35% semis/electronics, 25% automotive/EV, 20% aerospace, 20% industrials. For Q4, we guide $1.35-$1.40 billion total revenue, led by North America and APAC at 15-20%.

M&A remains a cornerstone of our growth strategy in an industry with supply chain headwinds, raw material escalation, and Industry 4.0 shifts. Industrials M&A volumes surged 22% YTD per PwC, with $1.2 trillion private equity dry powder and EV/EBITDA multiples at 10.2x creating opportunities in automation, electrification, and digital twins. Our FY2023 pipeline has $2.8 billion deployable capital, $1.1 billion committed across three deals expected to add $650 million annualized revenue and be 15-20% EPS accretive net of integration.

The $850 million RoboTech Dynamics acquisition closed late July, bringing $220 million revenue growing 28% organically at 25% EBITDA margins. It catapults us into the $15 billion cobot market (35% CAGR per McKinsey), with $65 million synergies from shared R&D on Nexus PLC and AI path-planning, cutting cycle times 40% in aerospace machining. RoboTech's 60% North America and APAC plants hedge tariffs; we've secured $120 million cross-sell, including Tesla Gigafactory.

In August, $450 million for Precision Alloy Forgings secures $180 million revenue at 18% margins, covering 30% FY24 raw needs, slashing nickel volatility exposure. $45 million procurement synergies by Q4 2024 via Dayton co-location for wind turbines.

Q4 closes $250 million carve-out of Siemens' hydraulic systems, €140 million revenue targeting $8 billion electro-hydraulic market, filling 15% EMEA gap amid 8% capex crimp. Migrating to eDrive actuators cuts energy 35%; IP aids EU cybersecurity compliance.

These diversify: automation 32% revenue (from 25%), renewables 18% (from 12%). Integration capex $80 million funded at LIBOR+125bps; ESG via 25% CO2 cuts. Delivering 8% inorganic growth this year, targeting 12% 2024; pipeline robust for additive and edge computing.

On capital returns, our share repurchase program highlights confidence in our FCF amid moderating inflation and North American demand. February's $500 million authorization through FY2025 builds on 2023's $300 million, repurchasing 3.8 million shares at $72.50 average. YTD current program: $215 million or 2.6 million shares at $82.70, 43% utilized.

Q1 $45 million, Q2 $60 million on price dips, Q3 $110 million from 18% aftermarket growth to $285 million (28% revenue). YTD FCF $420 million, 12% ahead; repurchases 51%. 85% open-market via 10b5-1; July ASR $75 million at $78 effective.

Reduced shares 1.8% to 159 million, adding 14 cents to Q3 EPS. Full execution boosts 2025 EPS $0.45; ROIC to 14.2%. North America (62% bookings) reshoring funds aggression; EMEA moderation preserves M&A dry powder. Tied to 4-6% FCF yield, net debt/EBITDA 1.2x. Q4 $90-110 million planned.

Macro factors have bifurcated demand: bookings +1.8% to $2.4 billion. Fed rates at 5.25-5.50% dampened capex, book-to-bill to 1.05x, ISM PMI 47-49 hitting auto/heavy machinery 7%. Aftermarket +3% resilient.

Inflation sticky at +4.2% on inputs; Value Engineering 2.0 with composites preserved pass-through, +22% semis demand.

North America (52%) +6% on IIJA; Europe (28%) -9% on energy; APAC (15%) mixed, India +18%; ROW +10% oil/gas. Geopolitics delayed 8% shipments; reshoring positive.

Demand Resilience Framework: semis pivot, Industry 4.0 upgrades, $1.8 billion liquidity for bolt-ons. Q4 demand +1-3%; 2024 mid-single organic.

We reaffirm full-year guidance: revenue growth of 12% and EPS of $7.20-$7.40. Committed to dividends and repurchases.

Now, I will hand over to Lisa Patel, COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Patel (COO):
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've streamlined supply chain and efficiency. Key component inventory at 125 days forward supply, up from 65 days YoY, enabling 98% on-time fulfillment, 15-point QoQ gain. Backlog delays down to 14 weeks from 22, matching pre-pandemic, outperforming peers.

Asia-Pacific semis lead times 18-20 weeks from 52, via GlobalFoundries/India quals. Europe steel surcharges +12%; fixed offtake with ThyssenKrupp. North America: 25% Mexico shift cuts transit 40%.

Components: bearings +30% availability; hydraulics 8 weeks; dual-source PLCs. COGS +14%, passed 80% via pricing; 3% deferral.

$45 million Supply Chain Resilience: AI forecasting 92% accuracy, 200k sq ft Spartanburg fab insources 40% servos. Late diligence on Mexico actuator.

Stabilizing semis; exit year 130 days inventory, sub-12 week leads Q2 2025. Diversified footprint a moat for 2025 margin expansion.

Investing in automation/digital for capabilities; monitoring global chains proactively.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Doe (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of rising raw material costs on your profitability?

Michael Chen:
Good question, John. Rising raw materials like nickel up 45% YTD and steel surcharges have pressured COGS 14% YoY, costing 120 bps on gross margins to 38.2%. We've passed 80% through dynamic pricing on configured products—average order value steady at $1.2 million—and surcharges on long-lead items, similar to Caterpillar and Deere. Vertical integration via PAF covers 30% needs, locking procurement synergies. Inflation sticky at 4.2%, but Value Engineering with composites cuts TCO 8-12%, preserving win rates. Combined with aftermarket resilience, profitability on track.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jane Smith (Morgan Stanley):
What is your outlook for demand in the aftermarket services business?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, Jane. Aftermarket is a bright spot, now 28% of revenue up from 24%, with 18% YoY growth to $285 million in Q3. Predictive maintenance via Forge Cloud and remote diagnostics yield 15% attachment rates, cutting downtime 25%—key amid capex restraint. Resilient at +3% despite macro, providing FCF visibility. Expect continued mid-teens growth into 2024-2025, driven by Industry 4.0 retrofits on CNC fleets and cobot uptime contracts. Secular tailwinds in EV, semis, aero position it for outperformance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Bob Johnson (JPMorgan):
Can you provide an update on your progress in reducing lead times?

Lisa Patel:
Absolutely, Bob. We've made strong headway: delays now 14 weeks on TitanPro assemblies from 22 peak, with 98% on-time delivery. Inventory buffer at 125 days; semis MCUs 18-20 weeks, bearings/valves improved 30%/50%. Mexico nearshoring and dual-sourcing cut transit 40%; AI forecasting at 92% accuracy optimizes pulls. Spartanburg insourcing and potential Mexico M&A target sub-12 weeks by Q2 2025. Outperforming peers amid Red Sea/geopolitics.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in GlobalForge Equipment. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
